atoms.text: In 1995, Chicago, Illinois experienced an extreme heatwave that took the lives of several hundred people in less than a week. In response, the city introduced a climate change action plan to manage the impact of extreme heatwaves in the future.
They identified places in the city that should be specifically targetted with green infrastructure. Reflective roofing was also added to many buildings to reflect heat from the Sun.

To protect residents from heatstroke and sunburn, the city also increased the amount of shady areas. This included increasing the amount of trees, which also helped to lower temperatures by providing shade.
